step_text: Co-culture GFP LUHMES with astrocytes for 72 hours.

step_text: Culture primary human astrocytes in Human Astrocyte Media (AM) supplemented with fetal bovine serum (FBS), penicillin streptomycin, and Astrocyte Growth Supplement.

step_text: Treat astrocytes with 11 μg/ml of an IGF1R-specific monoclonal antibody, MAB391, for 24 hours to reduce IGF1R levels.
step_rationale: To study the effect of IGF1R levels on astrocyte support, astrocytes are treated with a specific monoclonal antibody.
span_chunk: To reduce IGF1R levels, astrocytes were treated with 11 μg/ml of an IGF1R-specific monoclonal antibody, MAB391 (R&D Systems, MN, USA), for 24 h.

step_text: Wash the treated astrocytes with 1× PBS and culture them for a further 72 hours in fresh F10:MEMα media.
step_rationale: After antibody treatment, cells need to be washed to remove any unbound antibodies and cultured in fresh media to recover.
span_chunk: After 24 h, cells were washed with 1 × PBS and cells were cultured for a further 72 h in fresh F10:MEMα media.

step_text: Co-culture the treated astrocytes with GFP LUHMES on fibronectin-coated plates, following the strict differentiation protocol for LUHMES.
step_rationale: To assess astrocyte support for neuronal cells, co-culturing with LUHMES is necessary.
span_chunk: Astrocytes were co-cultured with LUHMES/GFP LUHMES based on the strict differentiation protocol of these cells.

step_text: Sort the MAB391/IgG-treated astrocytes co-cultured with GFP LUHMES by FACS using the FACS ARIA cell sorter, based on fluorescence and forward scatter (FSC)/side scatter (SSC) size dimensions.
step_rationale: FACS sorting allows for the separation of different cell types based on specific characteristics such as fluorescence and size.
span_chunk: To separate MAB391/IgG-treated astrocytes co-cultured with GFP LUHMES cells were FACS sorted and separated using the FACS ARIA cell sorter (BD Biosciences). Cells were sorted for fluorescence and forward scatter (FSC)/side scatter (SSC) size dimensions.

step_text: Discard cells with low fluorescence or overlapping SSC profiles to achieve enriched populations of astrocytes and GFP LUHMES.
step_rationale: Removing cells with low fluorescence or overlapping size profiles ensures the purity of the sorted cell populations.
span_chunk: Cells with low fluorescence or cells with overlapping SSC profiles were discarded in order to achieve enriched populations of astrocytes and GFP LUHMES.

step_text: Collect the sorted cells in Advanced MEM media, centrifuge for 4 minutes at 400 g (av), and then resuspend in TRIzol® for RNA isolation.
step_rationale: To prepare the sorted cells for RNA isolation, they need to be collected, centrifuged to pellet, and resuspended in a suitable reagent.
span_chunk: Cells were collected in Advanced MEM media, centrifuged for 4 min at 400 g (av) and then resuspended in TRIzol® (Life Technologies).

step_text: Obtain ethics approval for the use of human specimens.

step_text: Select lung postmortem biopsy specimens from eight patients at the University Hospital of Liege.

step_text: Select postmortem biopsy specimens from the liver, heart, kidney, and pancreas from two COVID-19 patients.

step_text: Obtain the last available blood sample from COVID-19 patients taken within 24 hours preceding the patient's death.

step_text: Measure the volume of the intersection between the red threshold and the green threshold using the second Imaris script/macro tool.

span_chunk: iSLK.219, iSLKTet-RTABAC16WT, and iSLKTet-RTABAC16RTASTOP cells were maintained in DMEM supplemented with 10% Tet-Free Fetal Bovine Serum with additional 600μg/mL hygromycin B, 400μg/mL G418, 1μg/mL puromycin.

step_text: Grow TRExBCBL1-RTA and BCBL-1 cells in Roswell Park Memorial Institute medium (RPMI) supplemented with 8% fetal bovine serum, 2 mM l-glutamine, 25 U/ml penicillin, and 25 μg/ml streptomycin.
step_rationale: To culture additional cell lines necessary for the assay.
span_chunk: TRExBCBL1-RTA and BCBL-1 cells were grown in Roswell Park Memorial Institute medium (RPMI) supplemented with 8% fetal bovine serum (HyClone, Logan, UT), 2 mM l-glutamine, 25 U/ml penicillin, and 25 μg/ml streptomycin.

step_text: Select and maintain BCBL-1 cells transduced with shRNA PRMT5 lentiviral vectors on 1μg/mL puromycin.
step_rationale: To select for cells that have been successfully transduced with specific shRNA vectors.
span_chunk: BCBL-1 transduced with shRNA PRMT5 lentiviral vectors (GE Dharmacon, Lafayette, CO) were selected and maintained on 1μg/mL puromycin.

step_text: Transduce BACmid-containing 293L cells with lentiviral vectors and maintain on 1μg/mL puromycin.
step_rationale: To introduce specific genes into 293L cells and select for successful transduction.
span_chunk: BACmid-containing 293L cells were transduced with indicated lentiviral vectors and maintained on 1μg/mL puromycin.

step_text: Generate constitutively expressing ORF59-Flag and dsRedORF59-Flag in 293L cells using a lentivirus system.
step_rationale: To create stable cell lines expressing specific tagged proteins.
span_chunk: Constituently expressing ORF59-Flag, and dsRedORF59-Flag in 293L cells were generated using a lentivirus system and ORF59-Flag expressing BACmid.

step_text: Transfect 293T cells with pLVX-ORF59-Flag or pLVXdsRed-ORF59-Flag lentiviral vectors along with packaging vectors to produce virions.
step_rationale: To generate lentiviral particles for transduction into target cells.
span_chunk: pLVX-ORF59-Flag or pLVXdsRed-ORF59-Flag lentiviral vectors were generated by introducing the gene into respective vectors, and transfecting into 293T cells along with the packaging vectors (CMV-dR8.2, pCMV-VSVG) for producing virions.

step_text: Add collected viruses to the target cells for transduction followed by selection with puromycin (2 mg/ml) to obtain a pure population of cells.
step_rationale: To introduce the lentivirus into target cells and select for cells that have stably integrated the viral DNA.
span_chunk: Collected viruses were added to the target cells for transduction followed by selection with puromycin (2 mg/ml) to obtain a pure population of cells.

step_text: Transfect BAC16 ORF59-Flag into 293L cells with Metafectene Pro followed by selection with hygromycin to obtain cells maintaining the KSHV BACs.
step_rationale: To introduce the BAC16 ORF59-Flag construct into 293L cells and select for cells maintaining the KSHV BACs.
span_chunk: BAC16 ORF59-Flag was transfected into 293L cells with Metafectene Pro as previously described [ 50 ] followed by selection with hygromycin to obtain cells maintaining the KSHV BACs.

step_text: Incubate all cultures at 37°C in a humidified environment supplemented with 5% CO2.
step_rationale: To provide optimal growth conditions for cell cultures.
span_chunk: All cultures were incubated at 37°C in a humidified environment supplemented with 5% CO2.

step_text: Perform LowCell ChIP using the LowCell ChIP Kit (Diagenode Inc.).
step_rationale: To perform chromatin immunoprecipitation on a small number of cells.
span_chunk: We performed LowCell ChIP using the LowCell ChIP Kit (Diagenode Inc.).

step_text: Fix 1 million cells as previously described, followed by a PBS wash and resuspension in the kit-provided chromatin-shearing buffer.
step_rationale: To prepare cells for chromatin shearing by fixing and washing them.
span_chunk: 1 million cells were fixed as described above followed by a PBS wash and re-suspending them in the kit-provided chromatin-shearing buffer.

step_text: Sonicate chromatin to an average size of 500bp using the Bioruptor Pico.
step_rationale: To shear chromatin to a size suitable for immunoprecipitation.
span_chunk: Chromatin was sonicated to an average size of 500bp using the Bioruptor Pico.

step_text: Precipitate chromatin with specific antibodies as previously described.
step_rationale: To isolate specific protein-DNA complexes from the sheared chromatin.
span_chunk: Chromatin with specific antibodies were precipitated as described above.

step_text: Extract DNA from chromatin bound to respective targets and their appropriate controls.
step_rationale: To prepare DNA sequencing libraries, it is necessary to first extract DNA from the chromatin that is bound to the targets of interest and the controls.
span_chunk: DNA extracted from the chromatin bound to respective targets and their appropriate controls was used for preparing the DNA sequencing libraries

step_text: Prepare DNA sequencing libraries using the NEXTflex TM Illumina ChIP-Seq Library Preparation Kit.
step_rationale: The extracted DNA is used to prepare libraries suitable for sequencing. The NEXTflex TM Illumina ChIP-Seq Library Preparation Kit is specifically designed for this purpose.

materials: NEXTflex TM Illumina ChIP-Seq Library Preparation Kit

step_text: Analyze the purity and quantify the mature libraries using Bioanalyzer 2100 and kappa library quantitation kit.
step_rationale: Before sequencing, it is important to ensure that the libraries are pure and to determine their concentration.
span_chunk: Mature libraries were analyzed for purity and quantification using Bioanalyzer 2100 (Agilent Technologies, Inc.) and kappa library quantitation kit (Kappa Biosystems, Inc.)

step_text: Sequence the libraries on Illumina NextSeq500.
step_rationale: Sequencing the prepared libraries is necessary to obtain the DNA sequence data for analysis.
span_chunk: Sequencing of these libraries was done on Illumina NextSeq500 (Illumina Inc.)

step_text: Analyze the sequences using CLC Workbench 10.0.1.

span_chunk: Transduced cells were selected with 1μg/mL puromycin...

step_rationale: To confirm the reduction of PRMT5 protein levels and mRNA expression, respectively, and to validate the effectiveness of the knockdown.

step_text: Culture 293L cells with either BAC36WT, BAC36Δ50, BAC36Δ59, BAC16WT, or BAC16RTASTOP.

step_text: Generate cDNA from the isolated RNA using a High-Capacity RNA-to-cDNA kit.

span_chunk: cDNA was generated using High-Capacity RNA-to-cDNA kit (Applied Biosystems Inc.) according to manufacturer’s instructions

step_text: Perform real-time qPCR analysis using the cDNA to amplify viral ORF targets.

step_text: Calculate fold changes in gene expression using the ΔΔCt method and represent the data with error bars indicating standard deviation of three experiment replicates.

step_text: Dispense siRNA SMARTpools into 384-well plates
step_rationale: To prepare the siRNA screen, the siRNA SMARTpools must be accurately dispensed into the wells of the plates.

parameters: Number of wells: Triplicate (implying three 384-well plates)

step_text: Seal the 384-well plates
step_rationale: Sealing the plates prevents contamination and evaporation of the dispensed siRNA SMARTpools.

step_rationale: Storing the plates at -80°C preserves the integrity of the siRNA SMARTpools until they are needed for the screen.
span_chunk: Plates were stored at -80°C until needed (minimum 24 h, maximum 48 h)

step_text: Thaw assay plates at room temperature.
step_rationale: Plates must be brought to room temperature to ensure proper conditions for transfection.

step_rationale: The transfection reagent is added to the assay plates to facilitate the transfection of cells.
span_chunk: 10 µl transfection reagent was added using a Multidrop 384 (ThermoFisher)

step_text: Count the Hela cells and prepare a cell suspension with a concentration of 3×10^3 cells in 40 µl.

span_chunk: Cells were counted and 3×10^3 cells in 40 µl
parameters: cell concentration of 3×10^3 cells in 40 µl

span_chunk: 3×10^3 cells in 40 µl were added to each well using the Multidrop 384

step_text: Incubate the plates for 48 hours.
step_rationale: To allow the transfected cells to grow and express the transfected material, a specific incubation time and environment are required.
span_chunk: Plates were incubated for 48 h at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2.

step_text: Remove media from plates by inversion.
step_rationale: The removal of media is necessary to prepare the cells for virus infection or control media application.
span_chunk: To infect, media was removed from plates by inversion,

step_text: Add 10 µl of media containing penicillin-streptomycin or virus to each well using the Multidrop 384.
step_rationale: The addition of media containing penicillin-streptomycin is for the control wells, while the virus is added to infect the experimental wells. The Multidrop 384 allows for precise and consistent dispensing of liquids into the wells.
span_chunk: and 10 µl media (as for transfection, but containing penicillin-streptomycin; Lonza) or virus (HSV-1-eGFP strain C12, diluted to MOI 0.5 in infection media) [34] was added using the Multidrop 384.
parameters: Volume of media or virus added (10 µl)

step_text: Incubate the plates at 37°C for 1 hour.

span_chunk: Plates were incubated at 37°C for 1 h

step_text: Add 50 µl of infection media to each well.
step_rationale: Additional infection media is added to ensure the cells have sufficient nutrients and to maintain optimal conditions during the infection process.
span_chunk: before 50 µl infection media was added
parameters: Volume of infection media added (50 µl)

step_text: Return the plates to the incubator.
step_rationale: Placing the plates back in the incubator allows the infection to proceed under controlled environmental conditions conducive to cell growth and virus replication.
span_chunk: and plates returned to the incubator.

step_text: Monitor eGFP fluorescence from 24 hours to 80 hours post-infection using the POLARstar OPTIMA plate reader.
step_rationale: Monitoring eGFP fluorescence allows for the assessment of virus replication, as eGFP is an indicator of viral activity.
span_chunk: Replication was monitored as a function of eGFP fluorescence from 24 h to 80 h post-infection using the POLARstar OPTIMA plate reader (BMG Labtech).

step_text: Calculate the virus replication slopes over the linear phase.
step_rationale: Calculating the replication slopes provides a quantitative measure of the rate of virus replication over time.
span_chunk: Virus replication slopes over the linear phase were calculated...

step_text: Normalize the calculated replication slopes to mock transfected wells on individual assay plates.
step_rationale: Normalization to mock transfected wells allows for the comparison of replication rates by accounting for any background fluorescence or variability in transfection efficiency.
span_chunk: ...and normalized to mock transfected wells on individual assay plates.

step_text: Add 5 µl of CellTiter Blue (CTB) reagent to each well containing transfected cells using the Multidrop 384.
step_rationale: The CTB reagent is used to determine the number of viable cells based on the fluorescent or absorbance signal it produces.
span_chunk: 5 µl CTB was added per well using the Multidrop 384.

step_text: Incubate the plates at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 for 2 hours.
step_rationale: The incubation period allows the CTB reagent to react with the viable cells to produce a measurable signal.
span_chunk: Plates were incubated at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2 for 2 h

step_text: Measure the fluorescence using the POLARstar OPTIMA plate reader.
step_rationale: Fluorescence measurement provides a quantitative assessment of cell viability.
span_chunk: before measuring fluorescence (POLARstar OPTIMA plate reader).

step_text: Normalize the fluorescence readings to the viability of mock-transfected cells, per plate.
step_rationale: Normalization to mock-transfected cells accounts for any baseline signal and allows for comparison between samples.
span_chunk: Readings were normalized to viability of mock-transfected cells, per plate,

step_text: Calculate the mean cell viability over three replicates.
step_rationale: Calculating the mean across replicates ensures the results are reliable and reproducible.
span_chunk: and mean cell viability over three replicates was calculated.

step_text: Identify values of cell viability below 60% as cytotoxic.
step_rationale: A threshold is set to determine which siRNAs are cytotoxic based on their impact on cell viability.
span_chunk: values <60% were considered cytotoxic.

step_text: Clone the HSV-1 clone collection into the bait vector pGBKT7 using recombinatorial (GATEWAY™) and conventional cloning methods.
step_rationale: To generate bait constructs for the yeast two-hybrid assay, the HSV-1 genes need to be cloned into a vector that will allow them to be expressed in yeast.
span_chunk: The HSV-1 clone collection was cloned by recombinatorial (GATEWAY™, Invitrogen) and conventional cloning into the bait vector pGBKT7

step_text: Screen the bait vector constructs against a library pooled from 12,381 MGC clones in the pGADT7 prey vector using a semi-automated Y2H assay.
step_rationale: To identify potential protein-protein interactions, the bait constructs containing HSV-1 proteins are screened against a large library of human proteins expressed in the prey vector.

step_text: Collect human protein-protein interaction data from the specified databases.

step_text: Download the human protein-protein interaction data as of May 18th, 2010 from the databases.

span_chunk: Interactions between HSV-1 and human proteins were connected to a network of human protein-protein interactions (a total of 62,310) taken from the databases HPRD [78] (Release 9), BioGRID [79], DIP [80], MINT [30] and IntAct (downloaded May 18th 2010).

step_text: Connect the HSV-1 protein interaction data with the downloaded network of human protein-protein interactions.

span_chunk: Interactions between HSV-1 and human proteins were connected to a network of human protein-protein interactions (a total of 62,310) taken from the databases HPRD [78] (Release 9), BioGRID [79], DIP [80], MINT [30] and IntAct (downloaded May 18th 2010).

step_text: Dilute the four individual siRNAs targeting different regions of each gene and a reconstituted SMARTpool to 0.3 µM in 1× siRNA buffer.

step_text: Carry out transfection and infection as previously described in the methods section.
step_rationale: To introduce the siRNAs into cells and challenge them with the virus to observe the effects on replication.

step_text: Calculate and normalize the replication slopes as previously detailed.
step_rationale: To quantify the effect of each siRNA on viral replication and compare it to control conditions.
span_chunk: Replication slopes were calculated and normalized as described

step_text: Consider the phenotype validated if two or more of the four siRNAs resulted in the same, or better, phenotype compared to the primary screen.
step_rationale: To confirm the reproducibility and specificity of the siRNA effects on the HSV-1 replication phenotype.

step_text: Lyse the cells in 100 µl TRIZOL reagent.

step_text: Acquire images of the cells post-infection using microscopy.

task_name: Kanamycin intein splicing reporter spot titers

step_text: Obtain the 3D structure of KanR (aminoglycoside-3′-phosphotransferase [APH(3′) Ia]) with PDB ID: 4FEW.
step_rationale: The 3D structure of KanR is required to analyze the context and properties of the +1 serine residues.
span_chunk: The three-dimensional (3D) structure of KanR [APH(3′) Ia; PDB ID: 4FEW]
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Identify all the +1 serine residues in the KanR structure.
step_rationale: The +1 serine residues are the focus for analyzing the intein insertion site characteristics.
span_chunk: analyze the context and properties of the +1 serine residues in KanR
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Calculate the relative solvent-accessible surface area (rSASA) for each of the +1 serine residues using PyMOL (version 2.3.2).
step_rationale: The rSASA provides information on how exposed or buried each serine residue is within the protein structure.
span_chunk: The rSASA for a residue is the solvent-accessible surface area of the residue in the context of the protein (taking into account its neighboring two residues) relative to a fully exposed residue.
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Determine the distance of each +1 serine residue to the dimer interface (DI) of KanR.
step_rationale: Understanding the proximity of the serine residues to the dimer interface can provide insights into their accessibility and potential functional implications.
span_chunk: The dimer interface (DI) is defined by all residues of the KanR subunits within 5 Å of each other in the dimer structure.
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Calculate the distance of each +1 serine residue to the active site (AS) of KanR.
step_rationale: The distance to the active site is important to understand the potential effects of the +1 serine residues on the enzyme's function.
span_chunk: The active site (AS) is defined by all residues of KanR within 5 Å of the bound kanamycin or ATP molecule in the structure.
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Calculate the number of amino acids between each +1 serine residue and the closest amino acid residue in the active site or the dimer interface.
step_rationale: The number of amino acids between the serine residues and the active site or dimer interface can indicate the potential impact on the protein's function after intein insertion.
span_chunk: the number of amino acids (AA) between a given serine residue and the closest amino acid residue in the active site or the dimer interface
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Measure the shortest distance in three-dimensional space (expressed in angstroms [Å]) between each +1 serine residue and the residues in the active site and the dimer interface.
step_rationale: The shortest distance in 3D space provides a precise measurement of how close the serine residues are to key functional sites of the protein.
span_chunk: the shortest distance in three-dimensional space (expressed in angstroms [Å]) between a given serine residue and the residues in the active site and the dimer interface
task_name: In silico analysis of KanR insertion sites

step_text: Grow M. smegmatis (MC 2 155) in standard 7H9 (liquid) and 7H10 (solid) media as a preparatory step before conducting spot titer assays.
step_rationale: Culturing the bacteria is essential to obtain a sufficient number of cells for the spot titer assays.
span_chunk: M. smegmatis (MC 2 155) was grown in standard 7H9 (liquid) and 7H10 (solid) media prior to spot titer assays.

step_text: Prepare the 7H10 media without albumin or catalase for the spot titer studies.
step_rationale: The specific media preparation without albumin or catalase is required for the spot titer assays.
span_chunk: For spot titer studies, 7H10 was prepared without albumin or catalase.

step_text: Perform two-fold dilutions of the M. smegmatis culture, starting from OD600 values of 3 to 5.
step_rationale: Diluting the culture is necessary to obtain a range of cell concentrations for the spot titer assay.
span_chunk: Two-fold dilutions, starting from OD 600 values of 3 to 5, of cells were spotted.

step_text: Spot 1.25 μl of each diluted culture onto the prepared 7H10 media.
step_rationale: Spotting the culture onto media allows for the observation of growth and determination of cell viability at different concentrations.
span_chunk: Cells present at 1.25 μl at each titer were spotted.

step_text: Incubate the spotted plates at 30°C for 5 days.
step_rationale: Incubation is required for bacterial growth and the development of colonies that can be counted for the spot titer assay.
span_chunk: grown at 30°C for 5 days.

step_text: Use the figure legends to determine the concentrations of cells, zinc acetate, and kanamycin used in the spot titer assays.
step_rationale: The figure legends contain specific details about the concentrations of each component used in the assays, which are critical for replicating the experiment.
span_chunk: The concentrations of cells, zinc acetate, and kanamycin used are described in the figure legends.

step_text: Grow overnight cultures of BL21(DE3) in LB broth.
step_rationale: To prepare the bacterial culture for overexpression of the MIG reporter.
span_chunk: For overexpression assays, overnight cultures grown in LB were subcultured 1:100 in fresh LB...

step_text: Subculture the overnight culture 1:100 in fresh LB broth.
step_rationale: To dilute the overnight culture for optimal growth conditions before inducing protein expression.
span_chunk: ...overnight cultures grown in LB were subcultured 1:100 in fresh LB...

step_text: Grow the subcultured bacteria to an OD600 of approximately 0.5 at 37°C.
step_rationale: To reach mid-log phase, which is optimal for protein expression induction.
span_chunk: ...grown to an OD 600 of ∼0.5 at 37°C...

step_text: Move the culture to 30°C and induce with 0.5 mM isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside (IPTG).
step_rationale: To induce the expression of the MIG reporter protein at a lower temperature, which can improve protein folding and solubility.
span_chunk: ...moved to 30°C, and induced with 0.5 mM isopropyl β-D-1-thiogalactopyranoside...

step_text: Allow protein expression to proceed for 1 hour.
step_rationale: To produce sufficient amounts of the MIG reporter protein for the assay.
span_chunk: ...and protein expression was allowed to proceed for 1 h.

step_text: Resuspend cell pellets in MIG buffer and lyse on ice using a tip sonicator.
step_rationale: To extract the MIG reporter protein from the cells by lysing them.
span_chunk: Cell pellets were resuspended in MIG buffer...and lysed on ice using a tip sonicator.

step_text: Pellet the samples at 20,000 × g and collect the soluble lysate for the assay.
step_rationale: To separate the soluble proteins from cell debris and insoluble material.
span_chunk: Samples were pelleted at 20,000 × g, and soluble lysate was assayed.

step_text: Take a time zero sample and store it at -20°C.
step_rationale: To have a baseline measurement of the splicing activity before any treatment.
span_chunk: A time zero sample was taken and stored at –20°C...

step_text: Incubate the sample lysate at 16°C for approximately 16 hours for M. smegmatis DnaBi1.
step_rationale: To allow intein splicing to occur under controlled conditions.
span_chunk: ...while the sample lysate was incubated at 16°C for ∼16 h for M. smegmatis DnaBi1...

step_text: Add zinc acetate at the indicated concentrations immediately prior to incubation.
step_rationale: To test the effect of zinc on intein splicing inhibition.
span_chunk: Zinc acetate was added at the indicated concentrations immediately prior to incubation.

step_text: After 1-hour incubation with zinc, treat the samples with a 2× excess of EDTA and incubate further as indicated.
step_rationale: To test the reversibility of zinc-mediated splicing inhibition by chelating the zinc ions with EDTA.
span_chunk: To verify that zinc-mediated splicing inhibition was reversible, following 1-h incubation with zinc, samples were treated with a 2× excess of EDTA and incubated further as indicated.

step_text: Purify M. smegmatis DnaBi1 using a chitin affinity column followed by gel filtration chromatography.
step_rationale: Purification is necessary to isolate the protein of interest from other cellular components to obtain high-quality crystals for structural analysis.
span_chunk: M. smegmatis DnaBi1 was purified using a chitin affinity column followed by gel filtration chromatography
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Concentrate the purified M. smegmatis DnaBi1 to 13 mg/ml.
step_rationale: Concentration of the protein is required to achieve the appropriate protein concentration for crystallization.
span_chunk: was concentrated to 13 mg/ml
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Grow M. smegmatis DnaBi1-zinc crystals using a hanging-drop vapor diffusion method by mixing 1 μl of DnaBi1 with 1 μl of reservoir solution.
step_rationale: The hanging-drop vapor diffusion method is a common technique for growing protein crystals by allowing the gradual equilibration of the protein solution with a reservoir solution.
span_chunk: M. smegmatis DnaBi1-zinc crystals were grown using a hanging-drop vapor diffusion method by mixing 1 μl of DnaBi1 and 1 μl of reservoir solution
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Prepare the reservoir solution containing 20% (vol/vol) 2-methyl-2,4-pentanediol, 0.1 M sodium acetate (pH 4.6), 0.2 M sodium chloride, and 2 mM zinc chloride.
step_rationale: The reservoir solution is critical for crystal growth and must contain the appropriate precipitants and conditions to promote crystal formation.
span_chunk: reservoir solution containing 20% (vol/vol) 2-methyl-2,4-pentanediol, 0.1 M sodium acetate (pH 4.6), 0.2 M sodium chloride, and 2 mM zinc chloride
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Allow the crystals to grow at room temperature for approximately 1.5 weeks.
step_rationale: Time is required for the protein molecules to arrange themselves into a crystalline lattice.
span_chunk: Crystals were grown at room temperature for approximately 1.5 weeks
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Transfer all crystals to a cryoprotectant solution containing the crystallization buffer with an increased MPD concentration of 30% before data collection.
step_rationale: Cryoprotection is necessary to prevent ice crystal formation that can damage the protein crystals during flash-cooling in liquid nitrogen.
span_chunk: Prior to data collection, all crystals were transferred to a cryoprotectant solution containing crystallization buffer with an MPD concentration of 30%
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Flash-cool the crystals directly in liquid nitrogen.
step_rationale: Flash-cooling the crystals in liquid nitrogen preserves their structure and prevents radiation damage during data collection.
span_chunk: The crystals were flash-cooled directly in liquid nitrogen
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Collect diffraction data for the DnaBi1-zinc crystals at 100 K at the F1 beamline of the Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source (CHESS).
step_rationale: Diffraction data collection at low temperatures reduces radiation damage and allows for the determination of the crystal structure.
span_chunk: Diffraction data for the DnaBi1-zinc crystals were collected at 100 K at the F1 beamline of the Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source (CHESS)
parameters: facility: Cornell High Energy Synchrotron Source (CHESS)
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Process the images in imosfilm (CCP4 version 7) and scale using Scala (CCP4 version 7).
step_rationale: Image processing and scaling are necessary to convert the raw diffraction data into a form suitable for structure determination.
span_chunk: The images were processed in imosfilm (CCP4 version 7) and scaled using Scala (CCP4 version 7)
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Solve the crystal structure of M. smegmatis DnaB1 intein-zinc by molecular replacement using Phaser (Phenix version 1.12-2829) with PDB ID 6BS8 as the starting model.
step_rationale: Molecular replacement is a method used to determine the phase angles for the crystallographic data by using a previously determined structure as a model.
span_chunk: The crystal structure of M. smegmatis DnaB1 intein-zinc was solved by molecular replacement using Phaser (Phenix version 1.12-2829) with PDB ID 6BS8 as the starting model
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Refine the structure using Phenix version 1.12-2829.
step_rationale: Refinement is the process of adjusting the model to best fit the experimental data, resulting in a more accurate representation of the protein structure.
span_chunk: The structure was further refined using Phenix version 1.12-2829
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Deposit the final refinement of the M. smegmatis DnaBi1-zinc structure with the Worldwide Protein Data Bank under PDB ID: 6OWN.
step_rationale: Depositing the structure in a public database allows other researchers to access and use the data for further research.
span_chunk: The final refinement of the M. smegmatis DnaBi1-zinc structure was deposited with the Worldwide Protein Data Bank under PDB ID: 6OWN
task_name: Crystal structure determination of zinc-bound DnaBi1

step_text: Input sequence to the array design.
step_rationale: The input sequence is the starting material for probe design.
span_chunk: Input sequence to the array design was 300 919 sequences, totaling 101.8 Mb, derived from the gene models predicted from the mapping of RNA-Seq reads... and de novo assembled RNA-Seq contigs.

step_text: Generate variable length probes (50- to 100-mers) at a 5-bp step across the entire sequence space.
step_rationale: Creating probes of varying lengths ensures coverage of the entire sequence space with sufficient resolution.
span_chunk: Variable length probes (50- to 100-mers) were generated at a 5-bp step across the entire sequence space.

step_text: Repeat-mask individual probes by removing probes with an average 15-mer frequency greater than 200.
step_rationale: Repeat-masking eliminates probes that are too common within the sequence, which could lead to non-specific binding.
span_chunk: Individual probes were repeat-masked by removing probes that had an average 15-mer frequency >200...

step_text: Compare the repeat-masked probe set to the target sequence using SSAHA with a minimum match size of 30 and allowing up to five indels or gaps.
step_rationale: This comparison is used to ensure that probes are specific to the target sequence and can tolerate minor sequence variations.
span_chunk: The repeat-masked probe set was compared back to the target sequence using SSAHA... using a minimum match size of 30 and allowing up to five indels or gaps.
parameters: Indels or gaps allowed: up to 5

step_text: Eliminate probe sequences with more than 25 matches in the target set from consideration.
step_rationale: Probes with too many matches could bind to multiple locations, leading to ambiguous results.
span_chunk: Probe sequences with more than 25 matches in the target set were eliminated from consideration.

step_text: Prepare two slides of the array design containing the probe set and random probes.
step_rationale: The slides need to be prepared with the probe set and random probes before hybridization can occur.
span_chunk: An array design was made using two replicates of this probe set, plus two replicates of a set of 77,192 random probes.

step_text: Label the barley cultivars with fluorescent dyes: Steptoe with Cy3 and Barke with Cy5 for the first slide, Morex with Cy3 and Bowman with Cy5 for the second slide.
step_rationale: Fluorescent labeling is necessary to differentiate the DNA of the different barley cultivars during hybridization.
span_chunk: Two slides of this array design were hybridized for 4 days with four barley cultivars (Steptoe (Cy3) versus Barke (Cy5), Morex (Cy3) versus Bowman (Cy5))

step_text: Hybridize the labeled barley cultivars onto the two slides of the array design.
step_rationale: Hybridization allows the labeled DNA from the barley cultivars to bind to the complementary DNA probes on the slides.
span_chunk: Two slides of this array design were hybridized for 4 days with four barley cultivars (Steptoe (Cy3) versus Barke (Cy5), Morex (Cy3) versus Bowman (Cy5))

step_text: Follow standard CGH protocols during the hybridization process.
step_rationale: Standard CGH protocols ensure that the hybridization is performed consistently and accurately.
span_chunk: using standard CGH protocols

step_text: Analyze the CGH results to identify probes with high signal intensity.
step_rationale: Probes with high signal intensity are indicative of missed repetitive elements that need to be removed to ensure the accuracy of the probe set.
span_chunk: Based on the CGH results, 0.42% of the probes were removed as missed repetitive elements based on high signal intensity.

step_text: Remove 0.42% of probes identified as missed repetitive elements from the probe set.
step_rationale: Removing these probes is necessary to prevent interference with the performance evaluation due to their high signal intensity.
span_chunk: 0.42% of the probes were removed as missed repetitive elements based on high signal intensity.

step_text: Identify probes that exhibit low signal for all four barley cultivars.
step_rationale: Probes that show low signal across all cultivars are likely to be contaminants or non-performing and should be excluded from the probe set.
span_chunk: An additional 2.16% of the probes were excluded as contaminants or non-performing, based on low signal for all four cultivars.
parameters: Criteria for exclusion (low signal for all four cultivars)

step_text: Exclude an additional 2.16% of probes that are identified as contaminants or non-performing.
step_rationale: Excluding these probes ensures that the remaining probe set is comprised of only those that are performing adequately.
span_chunk: An additional 2.16% of the probes were excluded as contaminants or non-performing, based on low signal for all four cultivars.

step_text: Prepare Illumina TruSeq Paired End libraries using genomic DNA and DNA Adapter Indexes.
step_rationale: The initial step in capture library preparation involves creating the DNA libraries that will be used for sequencing.
span_chunk: Illumina TruSeq Paired End libraries (Illumina Part # 15026486) were prepared essentially as described by the manufacturer (Illumina, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA) using DNA Adapter Indexes 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 or 12, respectively.

step_text: Fragment 1 μg of genomic DNA into a 200–300 bp size range.
step_rationale: Fragmentation of genomic DNA is necessary to create library fragments that are suitable for sequencing.
span_chunk: Briefly, 1 μg genomic DNA was fragmented into a 200–300 bp size range using a sample volume of 53 μl, Covaris microTUBES and a Covaris S220 Instrument (175 W ultrasonic power, 10% duty factor, 200 cycles per burst, 100 sec treatment time).

step_text: Perform size fractionation if necessary and recover DNA adapter ligated products with a size between 320 and 420 bp by excision from an SYBR-Gold stained agarose gel.
step_rationale: Size fractionation is used to select fragments of the desired size range for the library.
span_chunk: Libraries were utilized either with or without size fractionation. If size fractionation was used the DNA adapter ligated products were recovered with a size between 320 and 420 bp by excision from an SYBR-Gold stained agarose gel.

step_text: Purify the TruSeq DNA libraries using AmPure XP Beads and elute in Resuspension Buffer.
step_rationale: Purification is necessary to remove impurities and concentrate the DNA library fragments.
span_chunk: The TruSeq DNA libraries were purified using AmPure XP Beads (Beckman Coulter GmbH) and eluted in 30 μl Resuspension Buffer according to the manufacturer (Illumina, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA).

step_text: Enrich for correctly ligated DNA fragments by using 20 μl of the TruSeq DNA library as template in the pre-capture LM-PCR reaction.
step_rationale: The pre-capture LM-PCR is performed to selectively amplify correctly ligated DNA fragments, which will be used for hybridization.
span_chunk: To enrich for correctly ligated DNA fragments, 20 μl of the TruSeq DNA library were used as template in the pre-capture LM-PCR reaction (ligation-mediated PCR; 100 μl volume) containing Illumina sequencing adapters (2 μ m TS-PCR Oligo 1: AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGA and 2 μ m TS-PCR Oligo 2: CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAG) and 50 μl Phusion High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (2×, New England BioLabs GmbH, Part# F-531L).
parameters: Concentration of TS-PCR Oligo 1 and 2: 2 μ m each
Volume of PCR Master Mix: 50 μl

step_text: Add 10 μl of Roche NimbleGen's proprietary Plant Capture Enhancer (PCE) to a 1.5-ml tube containing 1 μg of the amplified sample library.
step_rationale: The Plant Capture Enhancer is used to enhance the hybridization process of the sample library.
span_chunk: Prior to hybridization 10 μl of Roche NimbleGen's (Madison, WI, USA) proprietary Plant Capture Enhancer (PCE) were added to a 1.5-ml tube containing 1 μg of the amplified sample library.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Add 1 μl of 1 mM TS-HE Universal Oligo 1 and 1 μl of the appropriate TS-INV-HE Index Oligo to the tube.
step_rationale: The TS-HE Universal Oligo 1 and TS-INV-HE Index Oligos are added to block the universal and indexed segments of the TruSeq DNA library adapters during hybridization.
span_chunk: Next, 1 μl of 1 mM TS-HE Universal Oligo 1 (AATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGCTCTTCCGATCT) and 1 μl of the appropriate TS-INV-HE Index Oligo (1 mM) were added.
parameters: 1 μl of 1 mM TS-HE Universal Oligo 1
1 μl of 1 mM TS-INV-HE Index Oligo
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Dry down the mixture in a SpeedVac at 60°C.
step_rationale: Drying down the mixture is necessary to concentrate the sample before hybridization.
span_chunk: The mixture was dried down in a SpeedVac at 60°C.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Pool up to six samples with different indexes for hybridization.
step_rationale: Pooling samples with different indexes allows for multiplexing and simultaneous processing of multiple samples.
span_chunk: Up to six samples provided with different indexes were pooled for hybridization.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Add 7.5 μl of 2× Sequence Capture (SC) Hybridization Buffer and 3 μl of Hybridization Component A to each dried-down sample.
step_rationale: The SC Hybridization Buffer and Hybridization Component A are required for the hybridization reaction.
span_chunk: To each dried-down sample 7.5 μl of 2× Sequence Capture (SC) Hybridization Buffer (tube 5) and 3 μl of Hybridization Component A (tube 6) were added.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Vortex the hybridization cocktail for 10 seconds and collect by centrifugation.
step_rationale: Vortexing and centrifugation are performed to mix the hybridization components thoroughly and to collect the sample at the bottom of the tube.
span_chunk: The hybridization cocktail was vortexed for 10 sec and collected by centrifugation.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Denature the sample in a heat block at 95°C for 10 minutes.
step_rationale: Denaturation is necessary to separate the DNA strands before hybridization.
span_chunk: Following denaturation in a heat block (95°C, 10 min) the sample was transferred to a 0.2 ml PCR tube containing 4.5 μl Exome Library (liquid array).
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Transfer the sample to a 0.2 ml PCR tube containing 4.5 μl Exome Library and incubate the hybridization sample at 47°C for 64–72 hours in a thermocycler with the lid heated to 57°C.
step_rationale: The incubation allows the sample DNA to hybridize with the probes in the Exome Library.
span_chunk: The hybridization sample (15 μl) was incubated in a thermocycler (lid heated to 57°C) at 47°C for 64–72 h.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Prepare Streptavidin Dynabeads for the affinity purification of captured DNA by vortexing, aliquoting into 1.5-ml tubes, and washing with Bead Wash Buffer.
step_rationale: Streptavidin Dynabeads are used to bind and purify the biotinylated DNA captured during hybridization.
span_chunk: Streptavidin Dynabeads (M-270, Invitrogen) were thoroughly vortexed, aliquoted (50 μl per hybridization) into 1.5-ml tubes and prepared for the affinity purification of captured DNA.
task_name: Capture library and liquid array processing

step_text: Prepare the LM-PCR master mix for amplification of the bead-bound captured library.
step_rationale: The master mix contains all necessary components for the LM-PCR reaction to amplify the library.
span_chunk: The bead-bound captured library was amplified using LM-PCR. LM-PCR master mix (200  5l volume) contained 50  5l of bead-bound captured library, Illumina sequencing adapters (2  5m TS-PCR Oligo 1 and 2  5m TS-PCR Oligo 2) and 100  5l Phusion High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (2 5, New England BioLabs GmbH, Part# F-531L).

step_text: Distribute the LM-PCR master mix into two 0.2-ml PCR tubes for amplification.
step_rationale: Splitting the master mix ensures that the reaction volume is appropriate for the PCR tubes and that the amplification is efficient.
span_chunk: Next, 100  5l of the master mix were distributed into two 0.2-ml PCR tubes for amplification.

step_text: Perform LM-PCR cycling with the following conditions: 98°C for 30 sec, followed by 16 cycles of 98°C for 10 sec, 60°C for 30 sec, and 72°C for 30 sec, then extend the DNA for 5 min at 72°C, and keep at 8°C until further processing.
step_rationale: These cycling conditions are designed to amplify the DNA fragments bound to the beads through multiple cycles of denaturation, annealing, and extension.
span_chunk: LM-PCR cycling conditions were: 98°C for 30 sec, followed by 16 cycles of 98°C for 10 sec, 60°C for 30 sec and 72°C for 30 sec. The DNA was extended for 5 min at 72°C and kept at 8°C until further processing.
materials: PCR tubes with LM-PCR master mix

step_text: Combine both LM-PCR reactions and clean them up using the Qiaquick PCR purification kit according to the manufacturer's instructions with slight modifications.
step_rationale: The cleanup step is necessary to remove impurities and excess primers from the PCR reaction to ensure a pure sample for subsequent analysis.
span_chunk: Both LM-PCR reactions were combined and cleaned-up using the Qiaquick PCR purification kit (Qiagen, Hilden) according to the manufacturer instructions with slight modifications.

step_text: Add 1 ml of Qiagen PBI buffer to each reaction, apply 600  5l of the sample in two consecutive steps to the same Qiaquick column, and centrifuge at 16000 g for 1 min.
step_rationale: The PBI buffer helps to bind the DNA to the column, and the centrifugation step ensures that the DNA adheres to the column matrix.
span_chunk: To each reaction (200  5l), 1 ml of Qiagen PBI buffer was added; 600  5l of the sample were applied in two consecutive steps to the same Qiaquick column (centrifugation 16000 g for 1 min).

step_text: Wash the column with 750  5l Qiagen PE buffer, discard the flow-through, and spin the column for 1 min at 16000 g. Rotate the column 180° and spin again for 30 sec to remove PE completely.
step_rationale: The PE buffer washes away any remaining impurities, and the additional spins ensure that the buffer is completely removed from the column.
span_chunk: Following washing with 750  5l Qiagen PE buffer, the flow-through was discarded and the column was spun for 1 min (16 000 g). In order to remove PE completely, the column was rotated 180° and spun again for 30 sec.

step_text: Elute the DNA by adding 50  5l pre-heated (to 50°C) EB, incubate for 1 min, and centrifuge at 16000 g for 1 min.
step_rationale: The EB buffer helps to elute the purified DNA from the column, and the heat helps to improve the efficiency of elution.
span_chunk: DNA was eluted after addition of 50  5l EB (pre-heated to 50°C), incubation for 1 min and centrifugation (16000 g, 1 min).

step_text: Record the A260/A280 ratio using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer and analyze the libraries electrophoretically using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with a DNA 7500 chip.
step_rationale: The A260/A280 ratio is an indication of DNA purity, and the electrophoretic analysis provides information on the size distribution of the library fragments.
span_chunk: The A 260 /A 280 ratio (1.7–2.0) was recorded using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer. Libraries were analyzed electrophoretically using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer (Santa Clara, CA, USA) and a DNA 7500 chip (Agilent Part# 5067-1506).

step_text: Map target regions derived from transcript contigs against the WGS assembly of barley cultivar ‘Morex’ using BWA and Mega BLAST.
step_rationale: To align the target regions with the reference genome and identify their positions.
span_chunk: Target regions derived from transcript contigs (full-length cDNA or RNA-Seq contigs) were mapped against the WGS assembly of barley cultivar ‘Morex’ with BWA (command bwasw) and Mega BLAST

step_text: Collapse mapping positions on the assembly into a single bed file using BEDTools.
step_rationale: To consolidate the mapping information into a standardized format for further analysis.
span_chunk: mapping positions on the assembly were collapsed into the single bed file with BEDTools

step_text: Map sequencing reads to the Morex assembly with BWA and compute coverage with SAMtools depth considering only properly paired reads.
step_rationale: To align sequencing reads to the reference genome and calculate the depth of coverage for each position.
span_chunk: Sequencing reads were mapped to the Morex assembly with BWA 0.6.2 (commands aln and sampe). Coverage was computed with SAMtools depth considering only properly paired reads.

step_text: Calculate coverage statistics with AWK scripts and visualize in the R statistical environment.
step_rationale: To analyze the coverage data and create visual representations for interpretation.
span_chunk: Coverage statistics were calculated with AWK scripts and visualized in the R statistical environment.

step_text: Perform regression analysis of sequencing output, read coverage, and the number of detected SNPs using standard R functions.
step_rationale: To determine the relationship between sequencing output, coverage, and SNP detection.
span_chunk: Regression analysis of sequencing output, read coverage and the number of detected SNPs was performed using standard R functions.

step_text: Compare regions with high coverage but not located within target regions with targets using Mega BLAST and filter BLAST output with an AWK script.
step_rationale: To identify and analyze regions of high coverage that may not correspond to the expected target regions.
span_chunk: Regions with high coverage but not located within target regions were compared with targets with Mega BLAST and BLAST output was filtered with an AWK script.

step_text: Call SNPs with SAMtools mpileup/BCFtools using default parameters and filter resulting SNP calls with a custom AWK script.
step_rationale: To identify single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the sequence data and filter out low-quality or low-coverage positions.
span_chunk: SNP calling was performed with SAMtools mpileup/BCFtools (version 0.1.18) using default parameters. Resulting SNP calls were filtered with a custom AWK script discarding positions with quality score below 40 or coverage below 10-fold.

step_text: Visualize SNP frequency along the integrated physical and genetic map of barley with an R script.
step_rationale: To display the distribution and frequency of SNPs across the barley genome.
span_chunk: SNP frequency was visualized along the integrated physical and genetic map of barley with an R script.
materials: integrated physical and genetic map of barley
