span_chunk: a TRACE GC 2000 equipped with an Rtx-5SIL mass spectrometer fused-silica capillary column (Restek; i.d. 0.25 μm, 30 m × 0.25 mm)
materials: Rtx-5SIL mass spectrometer fused-silica capillary column (Restek)

step_text: Use a TRACE DSQ quadruple mass spectrometer (ThermoFinnigan) for detection.
step_rationale: The mass spectrometer is used to detect and identify the scent compounds after separation by the GC.
span_chunk: a TRACE DSQ quadruple mass spectrometer (ThermoFinnigan)

step_text: Collect petunia flowers (line P720) 1 day post-anthesis (DPA) at 1500 h.
step_rationale: The specific developmental stage and time of collection are crucial for the consistency of the experiment.
span_chunk: Petunia flowers (line P720) were collected 1 DPA at 1500 h.

step_text: Excise detached corollas 1.5 cm below the limbs.
step_rationale: Excising the corollas at a specific location is necessary to standardize the sample preparation.
span_chunk: Detached corollas were excised 1.5 cm below the limbs

step_text: Place the excised corollas in a 150-μl solution containing 30 mM 2 H 5 -Phe stable isotope.
step_rationale: Incubating the corollas in a stable isotope solution allows for the uptake of the isotope for later analysis.
span_chunk: placed in a 150-μl solution containing 30 mM 2 H 5 -Phe stable isotope
materials: 2 H 5 -Phe stable isotope (98% purity, Cambridge Isotope Laboratories)

step_text: Obtain pBINPLUS plasmids carrying CaMV 35S-driven AnBGL1 coding for Aspergillus niger β-glucosidase 1, with or without lytic vacuole-targeting determinants (AnBGL1vac or AnBGL1cyt, respectively) cloned at the N-terminus.
step_rationale: The plasmids are required to perform the transient overexpression of AnBGL1 in petunia flowers.
span_chunk: Transient overexpression of pBINPLUS carrying CaMV 35S-driven AnBGL1 coding for Aspergillus niger β-glucosidase 1, with or without lytic vacuole-targeting determinants (AnBGL1vac or AnBGL1cyt, respectively) cloned at the N-terminus

step_text: Sequence the plasmids harboring the BGL1 constructs to confirm their validity for further use.
step_rationale: Sequencing ensures that the plasmids have been constructed correctly and are suitable for the experiment.
span_chunk: Plasmids harboring the BGL1 constructs were sequenced to confirm their validity for further use.

step_text: Subject petunia buds (line P720) 1 day before anthesis to vacuum infiltration with a mix of Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain AGLO carrying pRCS2-35S: GFP and bacteria carrying either pBINPLUS-35S: AnBGL1vac or pBINPLUS-35S: AnBGL1cyt in a 1:1 (v/v) mixture.
step_rationale: Vacuum infiltration is used to introduce the plasmids into the petunia buds for transient overexpression of the target gene.
span_chunk: Petunia buds 1 day before anthesis were subjected to vacuum infiltration with a mix of Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain AGLO carrying pRCS2-35S: GFP and bacteria carrying pBINPLUS-35S: AnBGL1vac or bacteria carrying pBINPLUS-35S: AnBGL1cyt in a 1:1 (v/v) mixture.

step_text: Use a control group where buds are inoculated with AGLO carrying only pRCS2-35S: GFP.
step_rationale: A control group is necessary to compare the effects of the transient overexpression with a baseline.
span_chunk: As a control, buds were inoculated with AGLO carrying only pRCS2-35S: GFP.

step_text: Three days postinfiltration (at 1500 h), examine the open flowers using a fluorescence binocular microscope under white and UV light with GFP filters to identify GFP-positive tissues.
step_rationale: Fluorescence microscopy is used to confirm the expression of the GFP marker, indicating successful infiltration and expression of the constructs.
span_chunk: Three days postinfiltration (at 1500 h), open flowers were examined using a fluorescence binocular microscope (FLOUIII, Leica Microsystems) under white and UV light with GFP filters.

step_text: Excise GFP-positive tissues and extract glycosylated scent compounds for GC–MS analysis.
step_rationale: The extraction of glycosylated scent compounds from GFP-positive tissues allows for the analysis of the effects of transient overexpression on scent compound production.
span_chunk: GFP-positive tissues were excised and glycosylated scent compounds were extracted and analyzed by GC–MS.

step_text: Grind 300 mg of tissue in liquid nitrogen.
step_rationale: Grinding the tissue in liquid nitrogen helps to preserve the enzyme activity by rapidly freezing the tissue, which prevents enzymatic degradation and maintains the integrity of the proteins.
span_chunk: tissues (300 mg) were ground in liquid nitrogen

step_text: Extract the ground tissue in 1.2 ml of 50 mM phosphate buffer with pH 4.3, containing 10 mM EDTA and 4 mM dithiothreitol.
step_rationale: The extraction buffer is used to solubilize the proteins from the ground tissue, and the specific components of the buffer (phosphate, EDTA, dithiothreitol) help to maintain the stability and activity of the enzymes, including β-glucosidase.
span_chunk: extracted in 1.2 ml 50 mM phosphate buffer pH 4.3, containing 10 mM EDTA and 4 mM dithiothreitol

step_text: Isolate protoplasts from petunia petals (line Blue Ray) following the procedure described by Faraco et al. (2014).
step_rationale: Protoplasts are required as the starting material for subsequent isolation of intact vacuoles.
span_chunk: Protoplasts were isolated from petunia petals (line Blue Ray) as described by Faraco et al. (2014).
task_name: Isolation of protoplasts and intact vacuoles

step_text: Assay protoplast viability using fluorescein diacetate solution.
step_rationale: Determining the viability of the protoplasts is essential before proceeding to isolate intact vacuoles.
span_chunk: Protoplast viability was assayed by incubating cells with 50 μg/ml fluorescein diacetate solution (Sigma Aldrich) in a 1:1 mixture (v/v) for 5 min prior to observation under the microscope.
task_name: Isolation of protoplasts and intact vacuoles

step_text: Observe the fluorescent cells under a fully motorized epifluorescence inverted microscope using a GFP filter.
step_rationale: Microscopic observation is used to confirm the viability of the protoplasts based on fluorescence.
span_chunk: Imaging of fluorescent cells was performed by fully motorized epifluorescence inverted microscope (Olympus-IX8 Cell-R) with a 12-bit Orca-AG CCD camera using a GFP filter.
task_name: Isolation of protoplasts and intact vacuoles

step_text: Isolate intact vacuoles from the protoplasts using a Ficoll step gradient with modifications from the method described by Robert et al. (2007).
step_rationale: A Ficoll step gradient is used to separate vacuoles from other cellular components after lysing the protoplasts.
span_chunk: Intact vacuoles were isolated from protoplasts as described previously (Robert et al., 2007) with some modifications.
task_name: Isolation of protoplasts and intact vacuoles

step_text: Precipitate aliquots of protoplasts and vacuoles in 10% (w/v) trichloroacetic acid.
step_rationale: To prepare the samples for western blot analysis, proteins must be precipitated from the protoplasts and vacuoles.
span_chunk: To extract proteins for western blot analysis, aliquots of protoplasts and vacuoles were first precipitated in 10% (w/v) trichloroacetic acid

step_text: Wash the precipitated samples with 100% acetone.
step_rationale: Washing with acetone helps to remove contaminants and excess trichloroacetic acid from the precipitated protein samples.
span_chunk: washed with 100% acetone

step_text: Resuspend the washed pellets in extraction buffer.
step_rationale: Resuspending the protein pellets in extraction buffer prepares them for further processing and analysis.
span_chunk: resuspended in extraction buffer (0.1 M Tris–HCl pH 8, 150 mM dithiothreitol, 2% v/v SDS, 2 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride, and 5% v/v β-mercaptoethanol)

step_text: Mix the supernatants with equal volumes of Tris-saturated phenol (pH 8) after centrifugation.
step_rationale: Mixing with Tris-saturated phenol helps to separate proteins from other components in the sample.
span_chunk: the supernatants were mixed with equal volumes of Tris-saturated phenol (pH 8)

step_text: Wash the phenolic phases with the extraction buffer, then with MeOH–ammonium sulfate (0.1 M) and 80% acetone.
step_rationale: Washing the phenolic phases with extraction buffer and then with MeOH–ammonium sulfate and acetone helps to purify the protein samples further.
span_chunk: the phenolic phases were washed with the extraction buffer, and 5 volumes of MeOH–ammonium sulfate (0.1 M) were added. Samples were washed three more times with MeOH–ammonium sulfate (0.1 M) and then with 80% acetone.

step_text: Resuspend the final pellets in NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer and incubate for 5 min at 55°C.
step_rationale: Resuspending the pellets in sample buffer and heating them prepares the proteins for electrophoresis by denaturing them.
span_chunk: The pellets were resuspended in NuPAGE LDS Sample Buffer (Thermo Fisher Scientific), and the tubes were incubated for 5 min at 55°C prior to electrophoresis.

step_text: Perform electrophoresis on NuPAGE 4–12% Bis–Tris gels.
step_rationale: Electrophoresis is used to separate proteins based on their size.
span_chunk: The samples were analyzed on NuPAGE 4–12% Bis–Tris gels (Thermo Fisher Scientific)

step_text: Transfer the proteins from the gels to iBlot nitrocellulose membranes.
step_rationale: Transferring the proteins to membranes is necessary for subsequent antibody-based detection.
span_chunk: Samples were transferred to iBlot nitrocellulose membranes

step_text: Block the membranes with skimmed milk-based blocking solution.
step_rationale: Blocking non-specific binding sites on the membrane prevents non-specific antibody binding.
span_chunk: following incubation with skimmed milk-based blocking solution

step_text: Incubate the membranes overnight at 18°C with primary antibodies.
step_rationale: Incubating with primary antibodies allows for the specific binding of antibodies to their target proteins.
span_chunk: membranes were reacted overnight at 18°C with the primary antibodies

step_text: Wash the membranes three times with Tween–Tris buffered saline.
step_rationale: Washing removes unbound antibodies from the membranes.
span_chunk: Following three 10-min washes in Tween–Tris buffered saline

step_text: Incubate the membranes for 1 h at room temperature with secondary goat anti-rabbit antibody coupled to horseradish peroxidase.
step_rationale: Secondary antibodies bind to the primary antibodies and are coupled to an enzyme that will produce a detectable signal.
span_chunk: the membranes were incubated for 1 h at room temperature in blocking buffer containing a 1:10,000 dilution of secondary goat anti-rabbit antibody coupled to horseradish peroxidase

step_text: Wash the membranes three times.
step_rationale: Further washing steps are necessary to remove any unbound secondary antibodies.
span_chunk: After three washes

step_text: Incubate the membranes with SuperSignal West Pico Chemiluminescent Substrate for 1 min.
step_rationale: The chemiluminescent substrate reacts with the enzyme on the secondary antibody, producing a light signal that can be detected by autoradiography.
span_chunk: the membranes were incubated for 1 min with SuperSignal West Pico Chemiluminescent Substrate

step_text: Develop the membranes by autoradiography using Image Quant Las 500.
step_rationale: Autoradiography is used to visualize the protein bands where the primary and secondary antibodies have bound, indicating the presence of the target proteins.
span_chunk: developed by autoradiography using Image Quant Las 500

step_text: Collect the data from the treatments that need to be compared for statistical analysis.
step_rationale: Before performing the Student's t-test, it is necessary to have the data that will be analyzed to determine the significance of differences between treatments.
span_chunk: Significance of differences between treatments were calculated by Student's t-test

step_text: Input the collected data into the SigmaPlot software v13.0 (SYSTAT).
step_rationale: The SigmaPlot software is the tool used for performing the statistical analysis, so the data must be entered into this software.
span_chunk: using the SigmaPlot software v13.0 (SYSTAT)

step_text: Perform the Student's t-test using the SigmaPlot software to calculate the significance of the differences between treatments.
step_rationale: The Student's t-test is the statistical method chosen to determine if there are significant differences between the treatments.
span_chunk: Significance of differences between treatments were calculated by Student's t-test

step_text: Interpret the results of the Student's t-test, considering a P-value threshold of 0.05 or less as statistically significant.
step_rationale: The P-value threshold of 0.05 is the standard cut-off for determining statistical significance in many scientific studies.

step_text: Obtain control and PLX5622 chow formulated in AIN-76A standard chow from Plexxikon Inc.
step_rationale: To prepare for the administration of the chow to the mice, the appropriate diet must be sourced.
span_chunk: Control and PLX5622 (300 ppm formulated in AIN-76A standard chow, Research Diets, Inc.) chows were provided by Plexxikon Inc (Berkeley, CA).
parameters: Concentration of PLX5622 in chow (300 ppm)

step_text: Ensure each C57BL/6J mouse ingests approximately 1.2 mg of PLX5622 per day.
step_rationale: To maintain a consistent dosage of PLX5622, the daily intake of the compound must be controlled.
span_chunk: Approximately 1.2 mg of PLX5622 was ingested by each mouse per day (calculation based on 4 g/mouse chow daily).

step_text: Administer the PLX5622 or control chow to 8-week-old C57BL/6J mice for 21 days.
step_rationale: The treatment period is required to assess the effects of PLX5622 or control chow on the mice.
span_chunk: Starting at 8 weeks old, C57BL/6J mice were treated with PLX5622 or control chow for 21 days.
parameters: Age at start of treatment (8 weeks)

step_text: Anesthetize the mice with an intraperitoneal injection of a ketamine and xylazine mix.
step_rationale: Anesthesia is necessary to minimize movement and stress of the mice during the irradiation procedure.
span_chunk: All the mice were anesthetized with intraperitoneal injection of a ketamine (100 mg/kg)/xylazine (10 mg/kg) mix

step_text: Place the anesthetized mice 16.3 cm away from a cesium-137 source.
step_rationale: Proper distance from the radiation source ensures that the mice receive the correct dosage of irradiation.
span_chunk: placed 16.3 cm from a cesium-137 source (JL Shepherd & Associates)

step_text: Shield the eyes and body of the mice with a lead collimator, limiting the beam to a width of 1 cm.
step_rationale: Shielding is crucial to protect non-target areas of the mice from radiation exposure.
span_chunk: The eyes and body were shielded by a lead collimator that limited the beam to a width of 1 cm.

step_text: Use an extra lead plate to block exposure of the trachea.
step_rationale: Additional shielding for the trachea prevents radiation damage to this sensitive area.
span_chunk: An extra lead plate was used to block exposure of the trachea.

step_text: Administer 1.65 Gy of irradiation on both sides of the head for each fractionated irradiation.
step_rationale: Administering a fractionated dose allows for accumulation of the total desired dose over multiple sessions, reducing acute toxicity.
span_chunk: Irradiated groups received 1.65 Gy of irradiation on both side of the head to accumulate 3.3 Gy for each fractionated irradiation.

step_text: Deliver three fractions of irradiation every other day over 5 days.
step_rationale: Fractionating the dose and spreading it over 5 days allows for the total dose to be accumulated while minimizing the potential for radiation-induced damage.
span_chunk: Three fractions were delivered every other day over 5 days to accumulate a total dose of 10 Gy.

step_text: Accumulate a total dose of 10 Gy over the course of the treatment.
step_rationale: The total accumulated dose of 10 Gy is the target for the experimental treatment.
span_chunk: to accumulate a total dose of 10 Gy.

step_text: House the mice in a room with reversed light cycle (12 light/12 dark) for at least 2 weeks before the tests.
step_rationale: To acclimate the mice to the environment in which the tests will be conducted.
span_chunk: All the mice used for the NOR test were housed in a room with reversed light cycle (12 light/12 dark) for at least 2 weeks before tests.

step_text: Handle the mice for 5 minutes each day for 5 days before habituation.
step_rationale: To reduce stress and acclimate the mice to human interaction prior to testing.
span_chunk: The mice were handled 5 min each day for 5 days before habituation.

step_text: Place an open arena (30 cm x 30 cm x 30 cm; L x W x H) in a dimly lit behavior test room with an overhead camera.
step_rationale: To provide a controlled environment for the mice to explore and to record their behavior.
span_chunk: An open arena (30 cm x 30 cm x 30 cm; L x W x H) was placed in a dimly lit behavior test room with an overhead camera.
parameters: 30 cm x 30 cm x 30 cm dimensions

step_text: Allow the mice to explore the open arena for 10 minutes for two consecutive days.
step_rationale: To habituate the mice to the open arena before introducing objects.
span_chunk: The mice were allowed to explore the open arena for 10 min for two consecutive days.

step_text: On day 3, place two identical objects in the arena and let the mice explore for 5 minutes.
step_rationale: To assess the mice's exploratory behavior towards familiar objects.
span_chunk: On day 3, two identical objects were placed in the arena and mice were allowed to explore for 5 min.

step_text: On day 4, replace one of the objects with a novel object and allow the mice to explore for 5 minutes.
step_rationale: To assess the mice's exploratory behavior towards a novel object and their ability to recognize novelty.
span_chunk: On day 4, one of the objects was replaced by a novel object and mice were allowed to explore for 5 min.

step_text: Record the trials using the overhead camera.
step_rationale: To capture the exploratory behavior of the mice for subsequent analysis.
span_chunk: Trials were recorded by the overhead camera.

step_text: Analyze the recorded trials using an automatic video tracking system for movement tracking or by manual scoring for exploratory behavior.
step_rationale: To quantify the exploratory behavior of the mice, particularly their interaction with the objects.
span_chunk: Trials were recorded by the overhead camera and analyzed by an automatic video tracking system (EthoVision, Noldus) for movement tracking or by manual scoring for exploratory behavior.

step_text: Define exploratory behavior as the animal directing its nose toward an object at a distance less than 2 cm.
step_rationale: To establish a measurable criterion for what constitutes exploratory behavior in this context.
span_chunk: Exploratory behavior was defined as the animal directing its nose toward an object at a distance less than 2 cm.

step_text: Secure the objects in the arena with magnets and wipe the arena and objects with 70% ethanol between trials to eliminate odor cues.
step_rationale: To ensure the objects remain in place during the test and to prevent the mice from using olfactory cues from previous trials.
span_chunk: Objects were secured in the arena with magnets. Arena and objects were wiped with 70% ethanol between trials to eliminate odor cues.

step_text: Prepare the modified Barnes maze with 40 escape holes.
step_rationale: The modified Barnes maze is the apparatus used for the DMP dry maze test to measure spatial working memory.
span_chunk: we used a modified Barnes maze with 40 escape holes (D = 5 cm, 16 holes on the outer ring with 50-cm distance to the center, 16 holes on the middle ring with 35-cm distance to the center, and 8 holes on the inner ring with 20-cm distance to the center).
parameters: Number of holes on each ring
Distance of holes from the center
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Cover all holes except for the escape hole, which should be covered with a dark escape tube.
step_rationale: The escape hole with a dark tube serves as the target for the mice to find, while the other holes are decoys.
span_chunk: All holes were uncovered with the exception of the escape hole, which is covered with a dark escape tube (a black PVC tube).
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Set the light to approximately 1200 lux and use a noise (2 kHz, 85 dB) during the test.
step_rationale: Proper lighting and noise are used to create a consistent and controlled environment for the test.
span_chunk: The light was set to approximately 1200 lux, and a noise (2 kHz, 85 dB) was used during the test.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Place visual cues on three sides of the maze.
step_rationale: Visual cues are used to help the mice navigate and remember the location of the escape hole.
span_chunk: Visual cues were placed on three sides of the maze.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Give mice four trials each day with an interval of 10 minutes between each trial.
step_rationale: Multiple trials with rest intervals are necessary to assess the spatial working memory of the mice over time.
span_chunk: Mice were giving four trials each day with interval of 10 min.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Place mice at the center of the maze under a dark box for 30 seconds before starting the trial.
step_rationale: The dark box is used to control the starting conditions for each mouse before the trial begins.
span_chunk: Mice were placed at the center of the maze under a dark box for 30 s.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Start the trial by removing the box and end the trial when the mice find the escape hole within 90 seconds.
step_rationale: The trial measures the time it takes for the mice to find the escape hole, which is indicative of their spatial working memory.
span_chunk: The trial started when the box was removed and ended when the mice found the escape hole within 90 s.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Guide mice to the escape hole by the experimenter if they cannot find it within 90 seconds.
step_rationale: Guiding the mice ensures that all mice have the opportunity to learn the location of the escape hole.
span_chunk: Mice were guided to the escape hole by the experimenter if they could not find it within 90 s.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Turn off the noise and cover the escape hole immediately after the mice enter.
step_rationale: Turning off the noise and covering the hole signals the end of the trial and prevents the mice from re-entering the escape hole.
span_chunk: Noise was turned off, and the escape hole was covered immediately after the mice entered.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Return the mice to their home cage after a 10-second delay.
step_rationale: A short delay before returning the mice to their home cage allows for a brief period of rest and consolidation of the spatial memory.
span_chunk: The mice were returned to their home cage after a 10-s delay.
parameters: Delay duration before returning to home cage
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Clean the maze surface and the escape tube with 70% ethanol (v/v) after each trial to minimize odor cues.
step_rationale: Cleaning the maze and escape tube prevents the mice from using scent cues to find the escape hole, ensuring the test measures spatial memory.
span_chunk: The maze surface and the escape tube were cleaned with 70% ethanol (v/v) after each trial to minimize odor cues.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Keep the escape tube at the same location and change it on each test day.
step_rationale: Maintaining the escape tube location during a single test day and changing it on subsequent days tests the mice's ability to remember and adapt to new spatial locations.
span_chunk: The escape tube was kept at the same location and changed on each test days.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Record the trials using an overhead camera.
step_rationale: Recording the trials allows for later analysis of the mice's performance and behaviors.
span_chunk: Trials were recorded by an overhead camera.
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Analyze the recorded trials using Ethovision software.
step_rationale: The Ethovision software is used to track the movement of the mice and analyze their performance quantitatively.
span_chunk: Trials were... analyzed by Ethovision (Ethovision, Noldus).
task_name: Performing delayed matching-to-place dry maze test

step_text: Perform the habituation phase on day 1 by placing the mice into an open arena for 5 minutes.
step_rationale: The habituation phase allows the mice to become accustomed to the open arena before the actual trials begin.
span_chunk: On day 1, the mice were put into an open arena (30 cm x 30 cm x 30 cm, L x W x H) for 5 min.
materials: open arena (30 cm x 30 cm x 30 cm, L x W x H)

step_text: Conduct trial 1 on day 1 by placing two identical objects at a distance of 28 cm from each other in the arena and allowing the mice to explore for 5 minutes.
step_rationale: This trial measures the mice's exploratory behavior with objects placed at a specific distance from each other.
span_chunk: On trial 1, the mice were put into the arena with two identical objects placed at a distance of 28 cm to each other for 5 min.

step_text: Perform trial 2 on day 1 with the same settings as trial 1 for 5 minutes.
step_rationale: Repeating the same settings as trial 1 ensures consistency in the measurement of exploratory behavior.
span_chunk: On trial 2, the mice were put into the arena with the same setting as trial 1 for 5 min.

step_text: Execute trial 3 on day 1 by shortening the distance between the objects to 14 cm and allowing the mice to explore for 5 minutes.
step_rationale: This trial assesses the mice's response to a change in the spatial arrangement of the objects.
span_chunk: On trial 3, the distance between the objects was shortened to 14 cm and the mice were allowed to explore for 5 min.

step_text: Allow a 3-minute interval between each trial and return the mice to their home cage after each trial.
step_rationale: The interval between trials provides a rest period for the mice and minimizes stress.
span_chunk: There was a 3-min interval between each trial, and the mice were put back into their home cage after each trial.

step_text: Repeat all trials on day 2 with the same settings as day 1, except change the distance between objects on trial 3 to 21 cm.
step_rationale: Repeating the trials with a different distance on the second day allows for the assessment of memory retention and spatial recognition.
span_chunk: One day 2, all trials were performed with the same setting as day 1 except that the distance between objects on trial 3 was changed to 21 cm.
parameters: 21 cm distance between objects on trial 3

step_text: Clean the objects and the arena with 70% (v/v) ethanol after each trial to minimize odor cues.
step_rationale: Cleaning with ethanol removes olfactory cues that could influence the mice's behavior in subsequent trials.
span_chunk: The objects and the arena were cleaned with 70% (v/v) ethanol after each trial to minimize odor cues.

step_text: Record the trials and score the total time exploring the object pair.
step_rationale: Recording and scoring the exploration time provides data for assessing hippocampal function based on the mice's exploratory behavior.
span_chunk: Trials were recorded, and total time exploring the object pair was scored.

step_text: Use the total time exploring during trial 1 on each test day as the baseline of exploration.
step_rationale: Establishing a baseline of exploration allows for comparison and analysis of changes in exploratory behavior across trials.
span_chunk: Total time exploring during trial 1 on each test day was used as baseline of exploration.

step_text: Euthanize the mice used for flow cytometry analysis and perfuse with ice-cold PBS.
step_rationale: Euthanasia is necessary to harvest the brain tissue, and perfusion with PBS is used to clear the blood from the brain to reduce background staining during flow cytometry.
span_chunk: The mice used for flow cytometry analysis were euthanized and perfused with ice-cold PBS.

step_text: Remove the brains from the euthanized mice and immediately place them into ice-cold HBSS.
step_rationale: Rapid transfer to ice-cold HBSS helps to preserve the brain tissue and cells for subsequent dissociation.
span_chunk: The brains were removed and immediately placed into ice-cold HBSS.

step_text: Dissociate the brain samples using a Neural Tissue Dissociation Kit (P) (Miltenyi Biotec).
step_rationale: The dissociation kit is used to break down the brain tissue into a single-cell suspension, which is necessary for flow cytometry analysis.
span_chunk: Brain samples were then dissociated using a Neural Tissue Dissociation Kit (P) (Miltenyi Biotec).

step_text: Place brain hemispheres in Golgi staining solution.
step_rationale: The initial step in Golgi staining is to immerse the brain hemispheres in the staining solution to allow for the uptake of the stain by the neural cells.
span_chunk: Brain hemispheres stayed in Golgi staining solution (A Modified Golgi-Cox Stain for Neural Cells, Docket No. D4433, Cornell University) for 14 days
materials: Golgi staining solution (A Modified Golgi-Cox Stain for Neural Cells, Docket No. D4433, Cornell University)

step_text: Transfer the brain hemispheres into 30% sucrose in ×1 PBS and store overnight at 4 °C.
step_rationale: After staining, the tissues are transferred to a sucrose solution to cryoprotect the tissues in preparation for sectioning.
span_chunk: were transferred into 30% sucrose in ×1 PBS overnight at 4 °C.

step_text: The following day, transfer the tissues into fresh 30% sucrose solution, protect from light, and store at 4 °C for at least 2 days.
step_rationale: The tissues are placed in fresh sucrose solution to ensure adequate cryoprotection and are protected from light to prevent degradation of the stain.
span_chunk: The next day, tissues were transferred into fresh 30% sucrose solution, protected from light and stored at 4 °C for at least 2 days.

step_text: Calculate the mean percentage of time spent on exploring each object during the NOR test.
step_rationale: To quantify the exploratory behavior of mice in the NOR test.
span_chunk: NOR test results are shown as mean percentage of time spent on exploring each object (time exploring familiar or novel object/total exploring time)...
parameters: time exploring familiar or novel object

step_text: Calculate the mean discrimination index for the NOR test.
step_rationale: To determine the preference for the novel object over the familiar one, indicating memory function.
span_chunk: ...or mean discrimination index ((time exploring novel object - time exploring familiar object)/total exploring time)...

step_text: Calculate the percentage of time spent on exploring both objects during trial 1 on each test day for the Metric distance test.
step_rationale: To evaluate the baseline level of exploration in the Metric distance test.
span_chunk: Metric distance test results are shown as percentage of time spent on exploring both objects in trial 1 on each test day.

step_text: Analyze the results for DMP and Metric distance tests using ordinary two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni's test for post hoc comparisons.
step_rationale: To statistically assess the effects of day and experimental group on the performance in the DMP and Metric distance tests.
span_chunk: Results for DMP and metric distance tests were analyzed with ordinary two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni's test for post hoc comparisons using day and experimental group as independent factors.

step_text: Analyze the results for NOR test, dendritic spine density analysis, and flow cytometry with PLX5622 and fWBI treatments using ordinary two-way ANOVA with Tukey's test for post hoc comparisons.
step_rationale: To statistically evaluate the impact of PLX5622 and fWBI treatments on the NOR test results, dendritic spine density, and flow cytometry outcomes.
span_chunk: Results for NOR test, dendritic spine density analysis, and flow cytometry with PLX5622 and fWBI treatments were analyzed with ordinary two-way ANOVA with Tukey's test for post hoc comparisons using PLX5622 and fWBI as independent factors.
